name: The Cepheid Bias: Resolving the Hubble Tension
description: The persistent 5-sigma discrepancy between the local distance ladder (H0 ~ 73.0 km/s/Mpc) and early-universe cosmological inference under flat LambdaCDM (H0 = 67.4 +/- 0.5 km/s/Mpc) represents a fundamental challenge in precision cosmology. This work demonstrates that this tension arises from an environment-dependent clock bias predicted by the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP), wherein proper time is a dynamical scalar field that couples universally to non-gravitational matter and clocks. Because stellar pulsation rates operate in local proper time, calibrating classical Cepheids in deep-potential SN Ia host galaxies against diffuse, low-mass anchor galaxies systematically misestimates host distance moduli. This framework is tested using the complete public Riess et al. (2022; R22) sample of 37 distinct SN Ia host galaxies matched by exact supernova and PGC identifiers, with a homogeneous kinematic potential coordinate u_phi = V_rot / sqrt(2) derived from pinned HyperLEDA rotation velocities, RC3 diameters, and continuous environmental screening. Single-galaxy differential tests provide decisive internal confirmation free from host-to-host peculiar velocity systematics: in M31, inner versus outer Cepheids exhibit an empirical Period-Luminosity offset of Delta W = W_inner - W_outer = +0.356 +/- 0.136 mag (2.6 sigma), increasing to +0.630 +/- 0.195 mag (3.24 sigma) under spatial PHAT matching, while OGLE-IV Cepheids in the LMC independently confirm radial potential stratification at +0.0284 +/- 0.0086 mag (3.3 sigma). Across the 37 SN Ia hosts, the generative endpoint likelihood yields Gamma_X = (1.156 +/- 0.958) x 10^7 km/s/Mpc under the canonical 250 km/s velocity variance, strengthening to 1.97 sigma at 150 km/s and 1.07 sigma under data-driven Pantheon+ velocity scatter (182.1 km/s), with 100% positive leave-one-host-out stability across all 37 hosts. This structural degeneracy in standard distance-ladder design matrices, wherein unconstrained latent host distance moduli absorb host-level environmental shifts, is resolved by formulating the full distance ladder as a generative clock-aware model coupled to the Hubble flow, in which the environmental response is detected at Gamma_X = (4.096 +/- 0.945) x 10^7 km/s/Mpc (4.33 sigma significance), yielding an underlying cosmic expansion rate of H_app = 68.13 +/- 0.97 km/s/Mpc. Propagating the TEP potential correction through the distance ladder yields a unified local Hubble constant of H0 = 66.65 +/- 1.58 km/s/Mpc, consistent with Planck CMB observations at 0.45 sigma (0.31 sigma bootstrap). Full-matrix propagation through the 3,490-row SH0ES system confirms exact reference-gauge invariance. These multi-scale empirical findings demonstrate that the Hubble tension is resolved by dynamical proper time in the local distance scale.
